1: Herb - The Lantern-Reed Beds: Tall reeds crowd the edge of a blackwater pool, their seed heads glowing faintly in the mist. Beneath them, medicinal leaves and pale fungi grow on hummocks above the waterline. Roll Herb Gathering Checks with Biome Advantage. The still water reflects the reeds like bars across a lantern-lit window.
2: Combat - The Sinking Chorus: 2d4 Husk Giant Frogs crouch among floating leaves, their throats pulsing with a wet, rhythmic croak. They spring from the shallows when the party draws near, splashing black water across the mud. Encounter: 2d4 Husk Giant Frogs (use Giant Frog stats; MM p. 325).
3: Vignette - The Bell Beneath the Water: A small bronze bell rings somewhere below the swamp's surface. Each note travels through the water and trembles in the party's boots. The reeds part around a patch of open water, but nothing breaks the surface.
4: Combat - The Drowned Log: What looks like a moss-covered trunk glides silently through the flooded brush. Then two amber eyes open above the waterline. 1d4 Husk Crocodiles surge toward the party, jaws snapping among the reeds. Encounter: 1d4 Husk Crocodiles (use Crocodile stats; MM p. 320).
5: Environment - The Siltwater Spring: Clear water bubbles through a bed of pale sand beneath the murky surface. Collecting water and edible marsh plants requires a DC 12 Survival check to restore 1d4 Rations. The pool is ringed with old hoofprints and the drowned remains of a fence.
6: Combat - The Mire's Heart: The insects fall silent, and bubbles rise from a patch of mud with no visible source. A Hollow unfolds from the waterlogged roots, bearing a Wetlands biome mutation and one additional randomly determined mutation. Encounter: 1 Hollow (Homebrew).
7: Environment - The Sunken Causeway: A line of dressed stones vanishes beneath the marsh, then reappears on the far bank. A DC 12 Investigation check reveals the safest route across. Success allows the party to travel an extra hex that day. Failure leaves the old causeway hidden beneath silt and floating weeds.
8: Environment - The Sucking Mire: The trail narrows to a strip of peat between pools of opaque water. Crossing requires a DC 13 Athletics check to keep moving through the suctioning mud. Failure: a traveler sinks and struggles free, taking 1d6 bludgeoning damage and losing 1d4 Ammunition and 1d4 Rations to the mire.
9: Combat - The Rootcoil: A broad-scaled shape slides down from a low branch, its body nearly indistinguishable from the water-dark bark. 1d4 Husk Giant Snakes strike from the overhanging limbs and coiled roots. Encounter: 1d4 Husk Giant Snakes (use Giant Constrictor Snake stats; MM p. 324).
10: Herb - The Bitterbloom Hammock: A raised island of peat supports bitter herbs, waxy flowers, and shelves of fungus. Roll Herb Gathering Checks with Biome Advantage. Dragonflies hover above the blossoms while the surrounding water lies perfectly still.
11: Combat - The Bog-Treader: A hulking shape pushes through the cattails, scattering waterbirds in a rush of wings. 1d4 Husk Giant Toads lunge across the muddy bank, their backs slick with black slime. Encounter: 1d4 Husk Giant Toads (use Giant Toad stats; MM p. 329).
12: Vignette - The Cypress Lanterns: Knotted cypress roots rise from the water like fingers. Between them, small blue lights drift at knee height, keeping pace with the party before vanishing beneath the duckweed.
13: Environment - The Broken Walkway: A rotting boardwalk crosses a deep channel, its planks swollen and bowed between half-sunken posts. Crossing requires a DC 12 Acrobatics check. Failure means falling hard against the submerged pilings and taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage.
14: Combat - The Reed-Cutter Pack: 2d6 Husk Giant Lizards burst through the reeds, using the shallow channels to circle the party. Their claws score the old cypress knees as they close in from several directions. Encounter: 2d6 Husk Giant Lizards (use Giant Lizard stats; MM p. 326).
15: Vignette - The Drowned Homestead: A roofline barely breaks the surface of a wide, still pool. A porch post leans beneath the water, wrapped in faded ribbon; something knocks softly from inside the submerged house whenever the wind shifts.
16: Combat - The Sunken Toll: A battered handcart blocks the old marsh road, its wheels sunk to the hubs. As the party approaches, 1d4 Husk Bandits and 1 Husk Captain rise from concealment behind the cattails. Encounter: 1d4 Husk Bandits + 1 Husk Captain. A DC 14 Survival check reveals their abandoned hideout, containing three Pre-Sundering Luxury Goods and 1d4 x 10 GP.
17: Environment - The Root-Caught Cache: A supply crate is wedged between the roots of a fallen cypress, its lid held shut by silt and swollen wood. A DC 13 Investigation check reveals a hidden cache of 1d4 Rations and a Pre-Sundering Luxury Good.
18: Herb - The Glasswater Fen: Silver-veined marsh plants grow around a spring as clear as glass. Roll Herb Gathering Checks with Biome Advantage. Their roots thread through cool gravel beneath the tannin-dark water, untouched by the rot beyond.
19: Combat - The Leechfall: The water dimples all around the party, then erupts in a cloud of pale, blood-hungry bodies. 2d4 Veil Leech Swarms (Stirges) pour from beneath a mat of floating leaves and rush toward exposed skin. Encounter: 2d4 Veil Leech Swarms (use Swarm of Stirges stats; MM p. 370).
20: Vignette - The Heron's Vigil: A white heron stands motionless on a dead branch above the marsh. Its reflection in the water turns its head a moment before the bird does. When the party looks away, the branch is empty and the water is unbroken.
